arc.title: Session 28 — The World Above
arc.text: The company stands in the World Above, beyond the moon-membrane, where Session 27 left them. The fight is unresolved — the leaping predator (the giant bush-baby), the great cat (unengaged), and the leech-larvae remain. Open leads recovered so far: Amber Reach (glimpsed as a living city) and the mountain waterfall. Talis burns below.
arc.summary: Finish the fight at the moon's lip; find Inola; the Runt God cries and Mollthain answers. Ends on Mollthain's leap.

beats.title: Running order
beats.text:
[SET 24 Sep] Session 28 finishes the World Above and ends on Mollthain's leap. The rescue in the Amber Reach is Session 29.

- Open mid-fight at the lip of the moon. The fight is theirs to finish.
- Speaker starts picking up the gods' voices. Drop fragments through the session (the radio beat).
- They find Inola in the trees, a pupa feeding on her face.
- The Runt God cries out. Draz feels it first; Mollthain's voice comes over Speaker.
- The great cat stops watching and leaps down through the moon toward the Amber Reach.
- Close on the company at the lip, the Reach below. Optional stop at Ulmira's Falls first (the last beat).

beats.title: Where they stand
beats.text:
[NOTE] From the S27 chronicle. They are in the World Above at the lip of the moon, the rupture the Runt God came through. The world below is visible through it, with Talis still burning. Pinchie and Speaker are with them.

**Unstuck from reality** [SET]: every Hope spent and every Armor, HP or Stress marked counts double until they fix their footing in this world.

- Draz: senses run together; he can't tell where a body ends and the air begins.
- Heyou: turned solid and heavy, as if in a lead suit.
- Jamal: red heat-sight (he saw the leech-things in the trees and a larger shape deeper in) and a rising fury.
- Sylvie: the Splendor back in her feels unearned; a strong pull forward and up, stronger than the pull home.

**Sylvie's sight**: from the lip she can see the world below clearly enough to set a door anywhere on it she can hold in her mind. Getting home is not the problem.

**PCs** [OPEN] Foundry snapshot of 12 Sep, two days after S27; check against the end of the session. The doubling makes Jamal's single Hope thin.

- Draz: 2 HP marked · Stress 3/6 · Hope 2 · last seen in his Legendary Beast shape (a Kodiak)
- Heyou: 0 HP marked · Stress 1/6 · Hope 1
- Jamal: 3 of 8 HP marked · Stress 3/6 · Hope 1
- Sylvie: 0 HP marked · Stress 0/6 · Hope 6

**Carried**: the heart Heyou holds (it draws the motes; a bud weeps Splendor essence), the vial of essence Draz kept, the suppression amulet Jamal took back from Retta, the vault map (the waterfall and Amber Reach leads), the expedition log (Heyou).

beats.title: The fight, unfinished
beats.text:
What is still in it at the end of S27:

- **The leaping predator** (a house-sized bush-baby): tail sheared off, one eye blinded by Heyou's fire-fletched shot, taken past its Severe threshold by Jamal and Heyou's joined strike, marked for death by Sylvie. Still up.
- **Leech-larvae** high in the trees. Jamal saw them with his heat-sight.
- **The great cat**, big enough to carry the bush-baby like a mouse, watching from the trees. It has not joined. [MINE] It is Mollthain; see the wail beat.
- **The ambush-ray** fled skyward from Sylvie's Umbra. It could come back.

None of these has a book stat block. Add stand-ins here if you want the per-copy trackers. The doubling applies to everything they mark or spend.

beats.title: Speaker, the radio: fragments for this session
beats.text:
[SET 24 Sep] Speaker picks up fragments of the gods talking among themselves, not meant for the PCs. The voices and the reception rules are in Overview › Speaker, the radio.

[MINE] Fragments for this session. Drop them in when the table goes quiet, or right after a relevant beat:

- **Mollthain**: "The little one is crying." … "I will hold it. Nothing will reach it." (with the wail)
- **Ossa**: "He'll flatten half the Reach." **Tlellic**: "He did the same at the Deep." (Grithmaar Deep, Jamal's village)
- **Caranthalis**: "They cut down my tree to take a branch. As if the branch were the gift."
- **Ulmira**: "My waters still run. No one comes to drink." (the hook for the Falls)
- **Kreth**: "Nearly have it. Don't wait up."
- **Tlellic**: "One of the small bright ones climbed up. The grubs found her." (Inola, before they find her)
- **Brathis**: "The dark-hearted one is ripening." (Sylvie)
- Someone: "The thief's blood is up here again." (Draz; Otheidas himself is never on the channel)

Hold back "…who is listening?" for a later session.

beats.title: Inola and the pupa
beats.text:
[SET 24 Sep] Inola came up. She found a way to ascend and took it: the thing she took from the vaults in S23, which she used to open her door at the Astronomer's Spire in S24. One of the pupae is on her face, feeding on her.

- Where: in the trees where the leech-larvae wait.
- Draz's sight: the pupa is rooted in her, and her white-hot Splendor is draining into it.
- She preached that only the Elect ascend. Up here the Elect are food.
- [MINE] The cure is the Umbra. The World Above has none, and its creatures recoil from it (the ambush-ray fled Sylvie's Dread in S27). Only Sylvie can pull it off her. Ulmira's water won't help; the pupa isn't Umbral.
- [MINE] Her door only went one way. She needs Sylvie to get home.
- Her ask: the Athenaeum is her home. When Mollthain goes down, she begs them to follow.

[OPEN] What the pupa becomes if it is left on her. What exactly she took from the vaults.

[NOTE] Draz ate a slab of leech-grub in S27. Nothing has to come of it.

beats.title: The wail and the leap
beats.text:
[SET 24 Sep] The Runt God cries out, wanting them back, and Mollthain answers.

- The Runt God is at the Celsian Athenaeum's pyre in the Amber Reach, where it was left with Ash-begets-Tide in S25 as the pyre's leash and fuel.
- Draz hears it first, through his bond.
- [MINE] The great cat is Mollthain. Valghast, the winged lion, is tied to Mollthain, and the sphinx carcass is lion-bodied. It stops watching and goes past them, down through the moon.
- Mollthain's idea of rescue is a wall around the little one. At a god's size that tears the compound apart: Session 29.
- Jamal: this is the god whose creature destroyed his village in Grithmaar Deep.

End on the leap, or on Sylvie opening a door to the Reach.

beats.title: Optional: Ulmira's Falls before going down
beats.text: [MINE] If they want an edge before the rescue, Sylvie has the lead: the high-country waterfall from the vault map. Its water destroys Umbral things on contact, which matters if the Athenaeum's pyre fails and the dead rise. Details in Places › Ulmira's Falls. Skip it if the table wants to go straight down.

arc.title: Session 29 — Rescue in the Amber Reach
arc.summary: Mollthain has come down on the Celsian Athenaeum to shelter the Runt God. Get the people out, keep the pyre alive, turn the god aside.
arc.text: [SET 24 Sep] The plan for Session 29. Settle the details after Session 28 is played.

beats.title: The situation
beats.text:
The Athenaeum was already weak. The scepter that fed its pyre was pulled in S21, the pyre-tower fell and the pyre sputters in the plaza, and the Runt God has been its leash and its fuel since.

Mollthain arrives to shelter the Runt God, and the Rampart shelters by walling in. Walls come up out of the Reach around the little god and cut the compound apart.

beats.title: Who needs saving
beats.text:
- Dagga
- Ash-begets-Tide, the priest of Ossa-in-absence who kept the Runt God company
- The remaining Celsians, students, and anyone sheltering in the compound
- The Runt God itself, depending on what the party wants
- [OPEN] Draz's father and twin siblings went west to the Amber Reach. Are they here?
- Inola has a stake: it is her home.

beats.title: Countdowns
beats.text:
[MINE]

- **The Rampart**: Mollthain's walls closing around the Runt God. When it fills, the compound is split and whoever is on the wrong side is cut off.
- **The pyre**: if the Runt God is walled off or taken, the pyre loses its fuel. When it fills, the Umbra comes in and the dead start to rise.
- **The Stacks**: the world's salvaged knowledge lies in the walls' path. Saving the books or saving the people.

[OPEN] Sizes. Speaker's reception of Mollthain gets louder as he closes, and can stand in for the Rampart clock.

beats.title: Mollthain
beats.text:
He can't be fought. Run him as an Environment and a countdown, not an adversary.

- Wants: to hold the little one safe. Nothing else.
- Voice: slow, few words, parental; walls and holding.
- Ways to turn him: Draz's bond with the Runt God; Jamal's grievance; Speaker, if someone finds a way to talk back; the Runt God quieting.

[OPEN] Write him up as a Daggerheart Environment.

beats.title: Rhys
beats.text:
[NOTE] Last spoke with the company in S18 (12 Mar), by the fire during the long rest after the eldritch thing went into the ground. Kaelyn was dead. At the start of S19 Sylvie told him to f*** off and die and blinked the company to the Athenaeum, leaving him on the mountain. There was no reply.

- Undead. A fellow Stoneweaver from the Sundering, sent up to the World Above with the Runt God when Sylvie thrust the Heart of Stone skyward.
- He and Kaelyn drew their power from it up there. Kaelyn held its leash; Rhys says he doesn't have the rapport.
- Last seen wanting to find and wrangle the Runt God, and ascend again.

**In his own words** [NOTE] From the S18 transcript, lightly tidied.

On following Kaelyn:

> "Honestly, I didn't know what his intent was. I assumed he had cause, and so I followed blindly, I admit."

To Sylvie, about the Sundering:

> "What you did in response was so powerful, and transformative. I don't know how you did it. I would be very interested to learn about your arts and your power, because whatever you had back then dwarfed ours."

The Runt God:

> "We've been blessed by being in the world above. And we've been blessed again, because unbeknownst, I think, to us all, the Heart of Stone was in fact the Runt God, that had been too small and too weak to abandon this world with the others — until you thrust it up above. We've been drawing power from it, developing our arts with its power."

> "We believe that the other gods are preparing for their next Ascent, but we have no way of ascending with them. But perhaps with you, we could ascend again."

The argument:

> "Do you not understand that your world is a caul? Like afterbirth. You've been discarded. If you want to survive, we need to keep ascending with the gods."

> **Sylvie:** "This was your world too, right, Rhys?"
> **Rhys:** "It was. Past tense."

> "Look, I'm not arguing that I deserve it, or that you don't deserve it. But if you want a continued and flourishing existence, I suggest we get back up to the upper."

> "Well, for one, it's not plagued by the Umbra. And you have all the benefits of new civilizations that are starting, that are basking in the glory of the gods above. They're going to ascend again soon. That's what Kaelyn said."

> **Rhys:** "Look, would you rather save some or not?"
> **Sylvie:** "I think what you really want is to save yourself."
> **Rhys:** "I would like to be part of the 'some.' That's true."

**Why he matters now**

- [MINE] The Runt God's wail that brought Mollthain could bring Rhys too. He wants the Runt God, and it is at the Athenaeum.
- He has lived in the World Above. He knows what the company has just seen.
- His claims, checked against S27: no Umbra up there is true; they've seen it. "The gods are preparing for their next Ascent" fits Kreth going to fetch something, and Sylvie's pull forward and up. "New civilizations basking in the glory of the gods" hasn't been seen yet.
- [NOTE] The campaign's name comes from this scene: "your world is a caul."
- The last word between them was Sylvie's curse.

[OPEN] Does he show up in S29? If he does: a rival for the Runt God, a reluctant ally against Mollthain, or both.

overview.title: The Shape of the World
overview.text:
- **Cosmic revelation**: world served as "egg" for gods who have now hatched and departed
- The Apostasy: Otheidas was a Promethean figure, trying to use the Splendor domain to grow civilization in the Halcyon Domain. But this was never a possibility; he did not know, or refused to acknowledge, that the Halcyon Domain was a mere embryo that the veiled gods were parasitic upon, and would inevitably abandon.
- Ygva’s Plan
- Is collecting blessed branches, and other Splendor-touched artifacts to attempt to lure back and trap the gods.

**Splendor Domain:**

- The gods' own magical domain, their essence
- Largely absent from the world now because the gods departed
- What little remains are "vestigial effects" - echoes, remnants, old practices
- Sylvie accidentally learned to tap into these remnants when rebuilding her magic

**Dread Domain:**

- Associated with the Umbra
- The magic that witches use (hence their stigmatization)
- The "dark" counterpart to Splendor's divine light
- THIS is what filled the void in Sylvie when Ygva took her Splendor

The Umbra crisis is happening *because* the gods took their Splendor with them when they left, creating a vacuum that Dread/Umbra rushed to fill,

**The Moon Connection**: Linked to Kreth (dark god of predation, long night, deception). The Moon rune "Jara" is Ygva's rune.

sections.title: Key Cosmological Points
sections.text:
**1. Concentric Sphere Structure (Jules Verne style)**

- The world is the interior of nested spheres
- The "sky" and "stars" are the underside of the next concentric layer
- Multiple eggs exist as different worlds
- Higher dimensional spheres represent new developmental stages

**2. Ontogeny Recapitulates Phylogeny**

- What inhabitants perceive as "history" is actually embryonic development
- Titans = skeletal framework (early development)
- Gods = organs/systems forming from that substrate
- Mortals/civilizations = late-stage cellular differentiation
- The "hatching" = cosmic entities reaching maturity and breaking out
- Current inhabitants are afterbirth—used-up developmental tissue

**3. Splendor Magic's Origin (The Apostasy)**

- Otheidas (god-king) was not part of the original clutch
- He wrestled with a developing god (Jacob and the angel) and drew blood
- That divine blood became the blessed branches
- ALL Splendor magic derives from this cosmic theft
- Otheidas tried to prevent birth/keep gods perpetually gestating
- It was always doomed—birth happens whether you want it or not

**4. The Moon**

- A hole into the next earth/dimensional sphere
- Not an object in the sky but a rupture between realities
- Sylvie's Splendor magic is gone because that chunk of earth literally exists in another dimension now
- She can't access it because it's in a different ontological plane

**5. Societies as Proteins**

- All civilizations, settlements, factions serve functional purposes like proteins in cellular development
- Temporary structures performing tasks during gestation
- Not conscious of their true purpose

**6. The Umbra is Entropy**

- Not evil or corruption
- The Second Law of Thermodynamics
- Inevitable disorder in a closed system after the organizational energy (gods) departed
- The pyres burn stolen divine energy to locally decrease entropy
- It's an unwinnable fight against physics itself

**7. No Access to the Beyond**

- No one can access or understand what "adult" stages, meaning, or procreation are for these cosmic entities
- The nature of existence beyond the outermost shell remains unknowable

sections.title: The Umbra - Deeper Truths
sections.text: The Umbra is not merely a realm of darkness—it is a source of power that connects to the old gods. Witches who draw from it gain abilities that mirror divine power but at significant cost. The corruption spreading from breaches like the one beside [Drosven's Gate](#atlas/drosvens-gate)'s plaza suggests the boundaries between worlds are weakening.

sections.title: Ygva's True Plan
sections.text:
[Ygva](#personae/ygva) seeks to gather remnants and totems of the gods to bind them in the [World Below](#atlas/world-below). She has recruited [Sylvie](#company/sylvie) as a "sister" in this endeavor, recognizing her Umbra abilities. Key elements:

- Collecting god-essences from various sources
- The [Askavir](#personae/askavir) heart contains potent Splendor magic
- [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)'s heart may be among offerings for the gods
- The binding would fundamentally change the world's divine order

sections.title: The Old Gods - Hidden Knowledge
sections.text:
**Tlellic (God of Predation)**

- The [Askavir](#personae/askavir) is his mount/avatar
- The Moon Rune symbolizes false hope and paralysis of thought
- Connected to the predatory cycle of the world

**Mollthain (The Rampart)**

- Left great creatures in [Grithmaar Deep](#atlas/grithmaar-deep)
- One such creature destroyed [Jamal](#company/jamal)'s village
- These creatures serve as guardians or weapons

**Otheidas (The God-King)**

- Relics protect against divine powers
- [Draz](#company/draz)'s amulet is one such relic (ineffective against Umbra magic)
- [Sylvie](#company/sylvie) possesses a circlet associated with him
- Connected to the [Celsians](#factions/celsians) and their knowledge

sections.title: The World Below
sections.text:
A barren expanse devoid of life beneath the surface world. Key features:

- Abandoned settlements
- Titans transporting massive rocks
- Stronger lunar augmentation for Umbra magic
- Potential prison for bound gods

sections.title: Kelun and the Stone Beings
sections.text:
[Kelun](#personae/kelun) is a figure of divine authority connected to stone constructs:

- Sensed a connection to [Heyou](#company/heyou)
- Expressed disappointment over the destruction of the [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex)
- May represent an aspect of the old divine order
- The [Living Fortress](#relics/living-fortress) and Stonewraiths are related entities

sections.title: The Heretic Marks
sections.text:
Both [Draz](#company/draz) and [Jamal](#company/jamal) bear heretic marks:

- [Draz](#company/draz): Inner bicep, concealed carefully
- [Jamal](#company/jamal): Right buttock

The marks identify them as heretics to something—likely religious or social order. The nature of their heresy and who hunts them remains to be explored.

sections.title: Heyou's Origins
sections.text:
[Heyou](#company/heyou) is more than a simple clank:

- A sigil on his chest indicates specific origins
- [Kelun](#personae/kelun) sensed a connection to him
- [Ygva](#personae/ygva) recognized him and could summon his detached leg
- A circlet matching his sigil exists among artifacts
- May be connected to the creation of new beings

sections.title: The Sacred Pyres - Mechanics
sections.text:
The pyres are more than magical fires:

- They anchor the barrier against Umbra
- Require [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch) from sacred trees to rekindle
- Connected to the divine order (trees guarded by beasts)
- Their extinguishing may be coordinated (the emergence at Drosven's Gate)

sections.title: Faction Secrets
sections.text:
**The Dimmers**

- Criminal network with extensive reach
- [Heyou](#company/heyou) is a member
- [Borek](#personae/borek) operates in [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step)
- Trade in valuable goods including [Askavir](#personae/askavir) eggs

**Goblin Engineers**

- Highly organized, not savage raiders
- Build fortifications and use explosives
- Corrupted by Umbra influence
- Defend territory in the caverns

**The Celsians / Celsian Athenaeum**

- Scholarly institution with arcane knowledge
- [Tamber](#personae/tamber) is a former initiate
- Knowledge of [Otheidas](#personae/god-king-otheidas) and protective relics
- May have information about the gods' binding

sections.title: Historical Timeline
sections.text:
**The Age of Titans**

- Predates known history
- Features throughout the Halcyon Domain demonstrate that titans must once have been present
- The titan skeleton near [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step) has been dead since at least the Apostasy
- Titans observed transporting massive rocks in the [World Below](#atlas/world-below)

**The Apostasy (~100 Years Ago)**

- The gods left the world
- The region was formerly known as the Halcyon Domain; no one now refers to it as such
- Around the same time, settlements began crafting sacred pyres, lit by [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch)es
- Umbral shadow has threatened all areas not graced by sacred pyres ever since
- Horrifying monsters lurk in the dark beyond pyre-light
- Death now risks blighting the soul, sometimes causing the recently deceased to threaten their former communities

**Recent Events**

- Something caused the pyre in [Drosven's Gate](#atlas/drosvens-gate) to spontaneously go out
- The cause is unknown, as is whether there is precedent

sections.title: Magic Systems
sections.text:
**Aetherweave (Wizards)**

- Source their magic from the vestiges of the Veiled Gods
- Some communities distrust this tradition

**Umbral Magic (Witches)**

- Used by witches who draw power from the Umbra
- Some communities distrust this tradition
- [Ygva](#personae/ygva) describes the gods as monsters and seeks to bind them

**Blessed Branches**

- At least one tree source exists
- The cause of their magic is unknown
- Their power in keeping the Umbra at bay is undisputed
- Required for starting sacred pyres

**Stone Constructs**

- Once served as mouthpieces of the gods
- [Kelun](#personae/kelun) is the primary known example

**Sylvie's Stoneweaver Origins**

- Originally a Stoneweaver sorcerer from the Stoneheart Peaks
- Stoneweaver order was hereditary, focused on earth energies, harmony, attunement, containment
- Five weavers were active, responsible for the Confluence Ritual:
- **Kaelen** hoped to seize control over the Earth-Heart; **Rhys** supported him
- **[Sylvie](#company/sylvie)** had begun to recognize a power within herself connected to "Sister Moon"
- A cataclysmic magical confrontation caused the Sundering of the Stoneheart, destroying the mountain settlement and blasting the peak (and presumably the Earth-Heart) into the sky to join the moon
- Kaelen and Rhys are presumed dead or on the moon
- The other two weavers are presumed dead, lost to the cataclysm
- Sylvie's magic ceased to operate, but she could travel safely in moonlight
- She slowly relearned magic traveling between settlements; some lore related to practices of the old Veiled Gods (Splendor domain) oddly seemed to work, even without divine connection
- Community was built around an ancient magical nexus
- "Sister Moon": She does not understand what this connection has to do with her, but has her theories

sections.title: Geography Overview
sections.text:
- Sacred pyres keep settlements safe from darkness; they're failing
- [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch)es required to rekindle/maintain pyres
- Settlements are scattered and operate semi-independently
- There is/was a vast region called [Amber Reach](#atlas/amber-reach) on the western side of the mountains

sections.title: Faeries in the Age of Umbra
sections.text: Faeries are more sensitive to the soul blight than other ancestries, causing their physical appearance to develop in jagged and monstrous ways. Where other peoples endure the Umbra through grit and Sacred Pyres, the faeries of [Thistleglass](#atlas/thistleglass) took a different path entirely.

sections.title: Thistleglass
sections.text:
[Thistleglass](#atlas/thistleglass) is a strange and magical forest in the southern coastal region of the Halcyon Domain, home to faeries, elves, and fauns. Few go in or leave. It is connected by road to [Redmorrow](#atlas/redmorrow) (a ruthless smuggler's haven built from grounded shipwrecks) and [Salthewn](#atlas/salthewn) (a coastal village that maintains black-pitch fires on buoys to ward off sea evils).

Thistleglass is tagged as **Forest / Mystical** — the only settlement with the Mystical designation.

sections.title: The Faeries' Response to the Umbra
sections.text:
The faeries of [Thistleglass](#atlas/thistleglass) were always strange and peculiar, but when the Umbra descended on the world, they did not resist it. They matched it. Every cruel thing ever imagined about the fae — the stolen children, the impossible bargains, the glamours that hide rot, the revelry that traps you for a hundred years — became literal truth. They didn't become mindless revenants. They chose this, or adapted to it with terrifying deliberateness.

They don't huddle behind Sacred Pyres. They don't endure. They simply decided the world is beautiful, and for them, it is.

sections.title: The Eyes of Kreth
sections.text:
**Kreth, the Veiled God**

[Kreth](#personae/kreth) is one of the dark gods of the pantheon, whose domains are **deception and the moon**. ([Tlellic](#personae/tlellic), the other dark god, governs predation and the long night.) Like all the Veiled Gods, Kreth abandoned the Halcyon Domain during the Apostasy. But Kreth left something behind.

**The Divine Remnant**

What [Kreth](#personae/kreth) left behind are **eyeballs** — divine organs of perception from the god of deception. Some of the faeries of [Thistleglass](#atlas/thistleglass) wear these eyes in place of their own. To receive the Eyes of Kreth, a faerie must gouge out their own mortal sight and fill the empty sockets with something divine and deceitful. It is a covenant written in flesh — a permanent choice to stop seeing the world as it truly is.

The eyes appear as pale, luminous orbs — little moons staring out from jagged, blight-twisted faerie faces. In the eternal gloom of the Age of Umbra, encountering a figure in the Thistleglass dark with two soft, cold lights where eyes should be is deeply unsettling. Not the warm glow of a Sacred Pyre. Something older and wrong.

**What the Eyes Do**

To see through [Kreth](#personae/kreth)'s eyes is to see the world as it can be *made to appear* rather than as it is. The faeries who wear them don't just gain power — they gain Kreth's perspective, his fundamental relationship with truth. Everything becomes malleable, negotiable, a surface to be rewritten.

**The illusions they create are real — for them.** When an eye-bearer reshapes the world, it *is* reshaped for them and for anyone caught inside it. The glamour doesn't just fool senses; it rewrites reality for those within it. If a faerie decides the path leads to a warm hearth and a feast, then you walk, and you eat, and you feel full. And maybe you are sitting in a bog slowly drowning. Maybe you're eating handfuls of mud and thorns. But within the illusion, it's real. The pain doesn't come through. The warmth is genuine. You are dying comfortably and gratefully.

There is no "seeing through" the glamour in any conventional sense. You can't disbelieve it. Dispelling it doesn't reveal the truth underneath — it destroys the reality you're currently experiencing and drops you into whatever is actually happening to your body, mid-consequence. Breaking free of a Thistleglass glamour might be worse than staying in one.

**The Hierarchy of the Eyes**

The Eyes of [Kreth](#personae/kreth) are divine remnants — limited in number, not something that can be manufactured. This creates a natural hierarchy within [Thistleglass](#atlas/thistleglass):

- **Eye-bearers** form an elite caste: a priesthood, a ruling court, or both. They are the ones who shape the glamours, enforce the bargains, and maintain whatever twisted order the forest runs on.
- **The rest of the fae** — those without the eyes — follow, serve, or fear the eye-bearers. Some may know exactly what is real and stay anyway.

**Thematic Parallels**

The Eyes of [Kreth](#personae/kreth) mirror other divine remnants left behind in the Halcyon Domain:

- **[Blessed Branches](#relics/blessed-branch)** carry splinters of [Caranthalis](#personae/caranthalis)'s divinity and can ignite Sacred Pyres
- **The [Askavir](#personae/askavir)** may be [Tlellic](#personae/tlellic)'s mount, pet, familiar, or avatar
- **The Eyes of Kreth** are a fragment of divine will tied to deception and the moon

Each represents a different god's lingering influence — and a different relationship between mortals and the absent divine.

sections.title: The Moral Problem
sections.text: The question the party will eventually face isn't just "how do we fight this." It's whether the faeries are even suffering. Whether breaking the glamour is rescue or cruelty. The faeries have built a paradise out of a god's refusal to accept what's true. Some of them may prefer the lie. Some of them may not even know it *is* a lie.

sections.title: Faerie Names
sections.text:
Faeries of [Thistleglass](#atlas/thistleglass) carry names that sound lovely until you sit with them — poetic, evocative, carrying a sense of something beautiful turned sharp or melancholy.

**Examples:**

- Winter's Fallen Leaf
- Thorn Beneath the Smile
- Evening's Last Whisper
- Hollow Where the Song Was
- Moth Against the Lantern
- Promise Left to Rot
- Dew on a Dead Branch
- Shadow Worn as Silk
- Silence After the Scream
- Lullaby for the Lost
- Needle in the Cradle
- Bloom That Drinks the Dark
- Sweetness on the Blade
- Web Across the Threshold
- Kindness Without Eyes

- The party has been heading southwest toward this region after leaving Witch's Peak.

overview.title: Vignette — The Whispering Deck
overview.text:
A little vignette for the Tarot, pre- Thursday:

Reaching into her worn leather pouch, Sylvie drew out her Whispering Deck. The cards hummed faintly in her palm. Perhaps, tonight, at last, they would be a mirror to the truths she sought. She shuffled, the dry rustle of the cards a familiar comfort, and laid out three for herself: Past, Present, Future.

The first card, turned for her Past, was the Tower. Sylvie’s lips thinned, a faint line of bitter frustration etched around them. Again. Always the Tower.

Its image was seared into her memory: a jagged tower struck by lightning, figures tumbling from its heights amidst chaos and ruin. To Sylvie, this card was the indelible mark of the Sundering. It wasn't just a symbol of destruction; it was the echo of her own hand in that destruction. It was the cataclysmic confrontation, the raw power that was unleashed, the moment she lost her connection to the Earth-Heart, the severance that still felt like a missing limb. The Tower was the smoking crater where her home once stood, the shattered fragments of her community, and the obliteration of her former self. It confirmed the profound, inescapable guilt that sat like a stone in her gut – a testament to her failure, her fear that her own power- what broken pieces remained of it- was inherently destructive, a burden that leveled all it touched. It was a constant finger in the wound of what she had lost, and what she had caused. As if she needed reminding.

Next, for her Present, she turned The Hermit. A sigh, barely audible, escaped her. Also predictable.

The Hermit depicted a cloaked figure, alone on a desolate peak, holding a lantern aloft. Her life since the Sundering. It spoke of solitude, introspection, and a deliberate withdrawal from the world. It was her chosen path of wandering, her avoidance of connection, and her relentless pursuit of forgotten lore. The Hermit's lantern represented her internal search for answers, her constant vigilance, and her self-imposed isolation. The card also spoke, albeit more quietly, to the profound grief she carried, the weight of a shattered past that dogged her steps, no matter how far she went. She was the seeker, but also the outcast, forever walking a solitary path. Her safest place was alone. Again - as if she needed reminding.

Finally, for her Future, the card was The Moon. Sylvie stared at it, her frustration deepening. It had been this way since the Sundering – a ceaseless cycle of these three cards, over and over.

The Moon card showed a winding path between two towers, leading towards the horizon where a full moon hung, shedding an eerie, uncertain light. Certainly, the Moon spoke directly to her new magic, but also, and more disturbingly, to mystery, intuition, and the unknown. Its light was deceptive, not illuminating truths directly, but revealing them through shadow and symbol. For her future, it meant a continued journey through uncertainty, endlessly navigating hidden dangers and illusions. Would her future forever be shrouded in uncertainty and isolation, never truly finding solid ground or clear light?

"Still the same," she murmured to the sleeping forest, the words barely a whisper. Years. Years of these same three cards, confirming her past catastrophe, her solitary present, and her mysterious, unsettling future. It was a truth, yes, but a frustratingly unchanging one - and one that only promised more danger, more ambiguity. Chaos, solitude, and endless mystery. Her future was all moonlit illusion. What she wouldn’t give to have a future defined by something other than solitude and uncertainty - and then she shut down that line of thought firmly. That, she decided, was enough self-pity for one evening, and put away the cards.

overview.title: Author's Notes — Age of Umbra
overview.text: *A spoken worldbuilding monologue by the GM, recorded 2025-10-17 (transcribed and lightly cleaned). These are author's-intent **lore revisions** made while developing the Age of Umbra campaign frame toward a Daggerheart campaign book in the style of the Root clearing books. GM canon — not player-facing.*

sections.title: The world as chrysalis
sections.text:
- The biggest revision concerns **[Otheidas](#personae/god-king-otheidas)**, the god-king: he was a **Promethean** figure. He tried to seize the power of the gods and build something lasting *here* — either not realizing, or refusing to accept, that the gods were always going to leave.
- The world is a **chrysalis** — a husk, embryological development. The **Titans** were the original stock: they built the preconditions, and out of the Titans came both the **gods** *and* the **ancestries** (shaped to help the gods develop). The world is a clutch of eggs.
- Now the gods have hatched and gone, taking most of the **Splendor** magic with them. What remains is **vestigial and dying**. The **[blessed branches](#relics/blessed-branch) are vestiges of [Caranthalis](#personae/caranthalis)**; other Splendor artifacts are tied to the other departed gods.
- The gods have withdrawn to a **higher sphere** — a **concentric-worlds** cosmology, very eldritch-abomination in flavor. The **Titans are now inert and buried**. The **Umbra bleeds through everything**; the sacred pyres, lit by Caranthalis's blessed branches, hold the Umbra at bay — an oil-and-water stalemate.

sections.title: The players
sections.text:
- **[Dimmers](#factions/dimmers)** — the criminal syndicate. Smaller players: they strip copper wire from the ruins of civilization. Nihilistic — *let's make a buck on the way out.*
- **[The Celsian Athenaeum](#atlas/celsian-athenaeum) and the Celsian itinerants** — wandering academic tutors who preserve knowledge and spread it between communities.
- **Witches** — wield **Umbra** magic. Some still cling to the old god-influenced **Splendor** traditions, but after a godless century those have become wonky hybrids; witches have largely gone all-in on the Umbra, making them a relatively new force. The most significant, for the party's purposes, is **[Ygva](#personae/ygva)**, the witch of **[Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step)**, high in the mountains.
- In those mountains the party brushes against vestiges of the veiled god **[Ulmira](#personae/ulmira)**, and against **[Tlellic](#personae/tlellic)'s** old familiar, the **[Askavir](#personae/askavir)** — a massive, Roc-like eagle-beast.
- The simiah largely rejected the sacred pyres and remained in the forests, not delving too far into things — except for one simiah community high in the mountains (**[Verrow's Span](#atlas/verrows-span)**).

sections.title: Why the gods left
sections.text:
- **The gods do not know why they left** — no more than a bird knows why it flies south before winter. It was a natural impulse, an inevitability, not a decision.
- To the extent that a god is sentient, it has built a **post-hoc rationalization** — a story that recasts the inevitable as a choice, so that leaving becomes something it *meant* to do.
- Whether a returning god would be resentful **varies by god**, and turns on the rationalization it settled into — but underneath every rationalization is the same blank fact: none of them chose, and none of them know.

*(GM: what rationalization did each god arrive at, and are those stories shared among the gods or divided up between them? This is the deeper question behind [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)'s "would the gods resent being called back" — and behind her own reach toward godhood.)*

overview.title: Speaker, the radio
overview.text:
[SET 24 Sep] Speaker works like a radio. It picks up fragments of conversations among the gods, not meant for the PCs, each god with its own voice.

[NOTE] What Speaker is: a faceless stone construct from below the Forbidden Library (S23). It woke to Sylvie's Umbra, not her Splendor. Stone constructs once served as the gods' mouthpieces (Kelun speaks for several). In S26 it raised Brathis's sign and answered to Brathis's name with "It is time."

[MINE] Reception:

- Receive-only.
- Clear in the World Above, where the gods are. Static back in the world below.
- A god's voice gets louder as that god gets closer. In Session 29, Mollthain's voice is the proximity clock.
- Kreth deceives: a fragment in one god's voice may be Kreth's. Heyou, looking through Kreth's eyes, might tell.
- Later: a god notices someone is listening.

[MINE] Voices:

- **Mollthain** (the Rampart): slow, few words, parental. Walls and holding.
- **Caranthalis** (the Tree of Light): warm, green, grieving. Speaks in seasons. Resents the tree-burners.
- **Ulmira** (pacts): formal and precise. Terms, oaths, breaches.
- **Kreth** (the moon, deceit): sly and playful, probably lying, always far off. He went to fetch something very large.
- **Brathis** (feral survival): guttural, present tense, all senses.
- **Tlellic** (the long night, predation): patient and hungry. Everything is prey.
- **Ossa** (the wanderer atop the peaks): airy, amused, half out the door.
- **Otheidas**: never on the channel. He was not of the clutch; the others call him the thief.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A large city on the western side of the mountains. Its current status is uncertain -- it is unclear whether it still stands or has fallen to the Umbra.

sections.title: History
sections.text: Amber Reach was a significant population center during the era of the Halcyon Domain. Its size and location suggest it was a major hub of trade and governance before the Apostasy.

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text: Amber Reach represents a potential westward expansion of the campaign. Its fate -- thriving, struggling, or fallen -- is yet to be determined and can be shaped to suit upcoming plot needs.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A settlement whose Sacred Pyre was extinguished when dark creatures emerged from the cracked ground beside the plaza. The party's starting point and the catalyst for their quest.

sections.title: Current Status
sections.text: The pyre went dark spontaneously. The cause is unknown, as is whether there is precedent for a pyre failing in this way. The settlement is currently in crisis, exposed to the Umbra and the monsters it brings.

sections.title: Connections
sections.text: - Road to [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step)

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text: The extinguishing of Drosven's Gate's pyre is the inciting event of the campaign. Whether this was natural degradation, sabotage, or something more cosmological remains a core mystery.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A vast subterranean expanse beneath the mountains, associated with dwarves. Features expansive caverns, deep tunnels, intricate stone formations, and a dark, foreboding environment.

sections.title: Climate
sections.text: Cool and damp due to underground nature.

sections.title: Significance
sections.text:
- Believed to house a great creature left by [Mollthain](#personae/mollthain), The Rampart
- Rich in resources but fraught with dangers
- Connected to sacred [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch)es and the [Old Gods](#factions/old-gods)
- Site of [Jamal](#company/jamal)'s past trauma (his village was destroyed by something here)

sections.title: Access
sections.text:
- Staircase begins at old temple near [Tern's Watch](#atlas/terns-watch)
- Moon Rune Carving provides view into [World Below](#atlas/world-below)

sections.title: Creatures
sections.text:
- Large flying mantis-like creatures with phasing quality
- The great creature of [Mollthain](#personae/mollthain) (unseen but referenced)

sections.title: History
sections.text: [Jamal](#company/jamal)'s crew encountered a massive creature here, prompting them to dig in different directions due to fear. This creature is connected to the destruction of his home village.

sections.title: Unique Properties
sections.text: Grithmaar Deep does not need a sacred pyre; the Umbra somehow doesn't reach it. The reason for this immunity is unknown.

sections.title: Jamal's Community
sections.text: [Jamal](#company/jamal)'s people were mining downward until they pierced through a shell-like boundary and glimpsed a massive monster deep in the earth, sleeping. They now only mine horizontally and refuse to go any deeper.

sections.title: Current Status
sections.text: Party confirmed intent to seek the great creature left by [Mollthain](#personae/mollthain). [Ygva](#personae/ygva) identified it as a viable target for acquiring god-touched artifacts.

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
Grithmaar Deep represents both [Jamal](#company/jamal)'s past trauma and a potential source of powerful artifacts. The creature of [Mollthain](#personae/mollthain) is a major plot element waiting to be confronted.

The phasing mantis creatures' wings can potentially be crafted into gliders—an option the party discussed but has not yet pursued.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A central feature in the plaza of [Drosven's Gate](#atlas/drosvens-gate), known for its solemn atmosphere. When lit, provides light and safety; when extinguished, plunges the plaza into darkness.

sections.title: Significance
sections.text: The magical flame is integral to the town's rituals and protective measures. Keeps the town safe from Umbra creatures and miasma.

sections.title: Current Status: EXTINGUISHED
sections.text: The pyre went out unexpectedly, triggering the campaign's inciting incident.

sections.title: Rekindling Requirements
sections.text:
- Ordinary fire will NOT restore its magic
- Requires a [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch)
- Party currently possesses one (hidden by [Heyou](#company/heyou) in [Living Fortress](#relics/living-fortress))

sections.title: The Extinction Event
sections.text:
When the pyre went out:

1. Plaza plunged into darkness

2. Massive chitinous creature burst from the cracked ground beside the plaza

3. Gelatinous creatures emerged

4. Party used smoldering embers for tactical advantage

5. [Draz](#company/draz) warned creatures regenerate without burning remains

sections.title: Aftermath
sections.text:
- Plaza remains dark
- Remnants of conflict litter the area
- Town is vulnerable to Umbra incursion

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
Rekindling this pyre is the party's primary quest objective. They now possess the [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch) needed but must return to [Drosven's Gate](#atlas/drosvens-gate) to complete the mission.

The extinction may not have been random—the emergence from the broken ground beside the plaza suggests coordinated action or weakening of protective barriers.

sections.title: Significance

- [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s hometown
- Known for syndicate activities

sections.title: Notable NPCs

The caverns beneath Salthewn are:

[Heyou](#company/heyou)'s past in Salthewn connects him to the [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) network. His knowledge of the flammable ooze (used in forge-fires) proved crucial during cavern battles.

The city's criminal underworld and [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s history there may provide plot hooks or complications as the campaign progresses.

sections.title: GM Notes
