sections.title: Description
sections.text:
A remote Ridgeborne settlement perched high in the mountains of the Halcyon Domain. Said to be the first step of a forgotten pilgrimage once walked in honor of the departed god [Ulmira](#personae/ulmira). The lower portions of massive carved stone steps are still visible; upper steps are lost beneath avalanche rubble.

A Sacred Pyre burns high in an exposed basalt cistern at the town's center, maintained as a beacon of safety and community. The pyre is still burning.

sections.title: The Kurael
sections.text:
The people of Ulmira's Step call themselves **Kurael**, meaning "those who endure upon the mountains."

**Language**

- **Lammat** is the primary dialect, shaped by the wind and stone of their mountain homes. Lammat lacks the consonants "p" and "b" entirely.
- **Kurethik** is an older ritual language still preserved and used in ceremonies. It predates the Apostasy.

**Ancestry Terms**

- **Shargan**: The Kurael name for themselves and other mountain-born Giants. Adults typically range from 5 to 10 feet tall, most often 7-9 feet.
- **Lenvar**: Humans; means "tide-chasers," referencing their fleeting, migratory nature.
- **Drakenn**: Dwarves; means "fire-sleepers," referencing their subterranean life and connection to heat and stone.

sections.title: The Askavir
sections.text:
A massive raptor-like being, seen in silhouette against the clouds or moon. Appears rarely -- at most once per month. Its name comes from the Lammat dialect. Rumored to have been the familiar of the Veiled God [Tlellic](#personae/tlellic). Its presence inspires awe and fear but it rarely attacks the Step directly.

See also: [Askavir](#personae/askavir)

sections.title: The Titan Skeleton
sections.text: At the mountain's base, just outside of Ulmira's Step near the road to [Drosven's Gate](#atlas/drosvens-gate), lies the remains of a massive titan clad in ancient metal armor. The skeleton is semi-buried, with teeth the size of a grown human and bones large enough to walk through. It has been dead since at least the Apostasy; rumors abound.

sections.title: Notable NPCs
sections.text:
- [Borek](#personae/borek) - [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) leader of local operations
- [Sarru](#personae/sarru) - Pyre-keeper

sections.title: Connections
sections.text:
- Road to [Drosven's Gate](#atlas/drosvens-gate)
- Part of the broader mountain settlements of the Halcyon Domain

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text: Ulmira's Step is the party's primary safe haven. The cultural details of the Kurael -- their languages, ancestry terms, and traditions -- provide rich material for roleplay encounters. The titan skeleton near the road is a landmark that hints at the Age of Titans and could hold secrets of its own.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A cliff-hugging village nestled in a mountainous region, characterized by unique architecture of dwellings carved from rock formations. Interconnected by rope bridges and ladders facilitating movement through steep, rugged terrain.

sections.title: Population
sections.text:
- Predominantly simiah (~30 original residents)
- A few human and Katari families
- Recently increased by refugees from [Dolm's Break](#atlas/dolms-break) (goblins, halflings, Katari)

sections.title: Notable Features
sections.text:
- Open areas for socializing and dining
- Sacred pyre at center for cultural rituals
- Makeshift morgue for sky burials
- Pool formed by rock formations (giant's open mouth shape)
- [Salthewn](#atlas/salthewn) architecture visible from vantage points

sections.title: Climate
sections.text: Harsh, cold, and misty. Snow near the peaks significantly impacts lifestyle.

sections.title: Notable NPCs
sections.text:
- [Akiri](#personae/akiri)
- [Janzi](#personae/janzi)
- [Tamber](#personae/tamber) - Celsian tutor
- [Bufa](#personae/bufa) - West-ranging explorer
- [Draz](#company/draz)'s great aunt (unnamed)

sections.title: Local Cuisine
sections.text: Thick worm steaks, powerful freeze-distilled liquor

sections.title: Connections
sections.text:
Routes to:

- [Tern's Watch](#atlas/terns-watch)
- [St. Thera's Remit](#atlas/st-theras-remit)
- [Dolm's Break](#atlas/dolms-break)
- [Amber Reach](#atlas/amber-reach) (ancient city)

sections.title: Recent Events
sections.text:
- Refugees arrived from [Dolm's Break](#atlas/dolms-break)
- [Askavir](#personae/askavir) attacked settlement, causing casualties
- [Sylvie](#company/sylvie) tethered [Askavir](#personae/askavir), causing crash into plaza
- [Ygva](#personae/ygva) arrived, sparked confrontations
- ~15 departed toward [Tern's Watch](#atlas/terns-watch) to distribute refugee burden
- [Askavir](#personae/askavir) body remains on wheeled platform for processing
- Party crafted ammunition and forged dagger from [Askavir](#personae/askavir) claw

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text: Verrow's Span serves as a sanctuary amid regional chaos. [Draz](#company/draz)'s connection to the simiah community here provides social capital. The [Askavir](#personae/askavir) remains are valuable and arrangements were made with locals for processing.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A cavernous realm accessible through a Moon Rune Carving. Characterized by a barren expanse devoid of life, featuring large stone-like structures and titanic beings engaged in construction.

sections.title: Climate
sections.text: Desolate, permeated by foreboding and ancient power. [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)'s lunar augmentation is notably stronger here.

sections.title: Inhabitants
sections.text:
- Titans engaged in construction (arranging stones for immense pyre)
- Automatons
- [Ygva](#personae/ygva) operates here

sections.title: Purpose
sections.text:
- Convergence site for mystical energies and remnants of the gods
- [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s plan: draw divine beings from upper world and bind them here
- Titans prepare offerings and construct massive pyre

sections.title: Access
sections.text:
- Through Moon Rune Carving
- [Ygva](#personae/ygva) and [Valghast](#personae/valghast) can transport others here
- Party landed on massive tower roof during descent

sections.title: Notable Features
sections.text:
- Abandoned settlements
- Titans transporting massive rocks
- Altars with artifacts
- Immense pyre under construction

sections.title: Key Events
sections.text:
- [Sylvie](#company/sylvie) observed titan through Moon Rune Carving
- [Valghast](#personae/valghast) responded to [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)'s fireball signal
- Party met [Ygva](#personae/ygva) here and learned her plans
- [Ygva](#personae/ygva) requested [Askavir Heart](#relics/askavir-heart) for her pyre ritual

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
The World Below is where [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s plan to bind the gods will culminate. The titans appear to serve her willingly or are compelled to aid in construction.

The party has agreed to help gather god-touched artifacts, making them complicit in [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s scheme. Whether this leads to salvation or catastrophe remains to be seen.

places.title: Ulmira's Falls
places.text:
[SET 24 Sep] The waterfall Sylvie found in her reading: high country, tied to one of the sites on the vault map. Its waters are blessed by Ulmira.

- Umbral entities are destroyed on contact with the water.
- Those who wield the Umbra are scalded, not destroyed. Sylvie is scalded.
- It has no aura. It protects only what it touches, so no settlement around it can function.

[NOTE] Heyou holds the log of the Athenaeum's expedition to the far guarded places, which lost sixty of its eighty.

[MINE] Ulmira is the god of pacts; the falls may be the last station of her forgotten pilgrimage, which began at Ulmira's Step. The ruin of a settlement that tried to live by the water: the dark came between the people and the falls at night, and their blighted dead still ring the water, unable to go near it.

[OPEN] Does carried water keep its power? (Suggested: yes, but finite; a vial destroys one Umbral thing or lays one blighted corpse to rest.) Is Speaker, woken on Umbra, an Umbral entity? Heyou's shadow-shape?

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A dwarf with a flamboyant, ostentatious style. Adorned with multiple rings, notably a heavy two-finger ring bearing the [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) emblem. Loud personality that makes him the center of attention at social gatherings.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Borek is the [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) Leader of [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step), operating in the shadows and tied to the underground dealings of the region. His welcoming demeanor allows him to facilitate deals effectively.

sections.title: Role
sections.text:
- [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) leader in [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step)
- Broker of information and valuable goods
- Connection to [Heyou](#company/heyou) through [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) network

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text:
- **[Heyou](#company/heyou)** - Fellow [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) member; possesses part of Heyou's essence
- **[Dimmers](#factions/dimmers)** - Leader of local operations

sections.title: Key Dealings
sections.text:
- Offered information about [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s missing limbs in exchange for [Askavir](#personae/askavir) eggs
- Hinted at possessing part of [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s essence
- Demanded [Askavir](#personae/askavir) ink in exchange for it

sections.title: Key Events
sections.text:
- Welcomed [Heyou](#company/heyou) with subtle signals of [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) recognition
- Proposed bargain involving [Askavir](#personae/askavir) eggs
- Entertained others publicly, providing opportunity for infiltration
- Party conducted stealthy infiltration into his quarters while he was distracted

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
Borek represents the criminal underworld's presence in [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step). His possession of part of [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s essence creates leverage over the clank.

His interest in [Askavir](#personae/askavir) eggs and ink suggests knowledge of their valuable properties. The infiltration into his quarters may have consequences if discovered.

As [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) leader, he likely has extensive knowledge of regional secrets and could be a valuable—if dangerous—ally or adversary.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A stone figure distinct from previous stone wraiths, identified as a mouthpiece of the gods. Possesses the ability to shapeshift, notably into [Mellon](#personae/mellon), a nearby ghost. Communicates telepathically with authority.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Kelun serves the divine pantheon, primarily speaking for [Caranthalis](#personae/caranthalis), the god associated with the [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex). He has also served Ossa Mollthain and [Tlellic](#personae/tlellic), indicating connection to a broader divine pantheon of eight gods, with [Otheidas](#personae/god-king-otheidas) representing cycles of life and undeath.

sections.title: Abilities
sections.text:
- Shapeshifting (took [Mellon](#personae/mellon)'s form)
- Telepathic communication
- Authority over stone constructs
- Serves as formal diplomatic envoy
- Can sense connections to other beings (sensed bond with [Heyou](#company/heyou))

sections.title: Role
sections.text: Beyond mere confrontation, Kelun serves as a formal diplomatic envoy in supernatural dynamics. He often departs to announce arrivals, showcasing authority and adherence to divine protocols.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text:
- **[Caranthalis](#personae/caranthalis)** - Primary god he speaks for
- **Ossa Mollthain** - Has served
- **[Tlellic](#personae/tlellic)** - Has served
- **[Heyou](#company/heyou)** - Sensed a connection, expressed disappointment
- **[Ygva](#personae/ygva)** - Compelled party to seek her

sections.title: Key Events
sections.text:
- Appeared on bridge after party destroyed [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex)
- Blocked party's escape, demanding they face consequences
- Shapeshifted into [Mellon](#personae/mellon), causing confusion
- Questioned party's failure to seek [Ygva](#personae/ygva)
- Stated: "My name is Kelun and you will follow me and we will decide what the consequences need to be"
- Revealed transactional perspective: party as "potentially useful components"

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
Kelun represents divine authority and judgment. His connection to [Heyou](#company/heyou) suggests the clank may have deeper ties to the divine order than realized. He operates on protocols that the party doesn't fully understand.

His disappointment over the [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex)'s destruction was genuine—the tree was sacred to [Caranthalis](#personae/caranthalis). The party remains in a precarious position with the divine powers.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A massive stone elemental approximately ten feet tall, composed of rock and earth with a rugged surface indicating natural origins. Resembles a giant stone construct adorned with intricate designs.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Connected to ancient Stoneweaver magic, the Living Fortress is controlled remotely via a pendant. Originally summoned by [Sylvie](#company/sylvie), control was later transferred to [Heyou](#company/heyou), who pilots it while remaining hidden from threats.

sections.title: Abilities
sections.text:
- Form manipulation
- Resilience against attacks
- Can relocate obstacles and opponents
- Shields allies from threats
- Controlled remotely via [Stoneweaver pendant](#relics/stoneweaver-pendant)

sections.title: Control
sections.text: The fortress's effectiveness is contingent upon the will of its controller. When the connection with [Heyou](#company/heyou) was severed after he unleashed a powerful smite, it became temporarily inert.

sections.title: Current Status
sections.text: Under [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s control. He hides the [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch) inside using [Phasing Vambraces](#relics/phasing-vambraces).

sections.title: Key Events
sections.text:
- Summoned by [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)
- Control transferred to [Heyou](#company/heyou)
- Relocated hooded figure blocking narrow bridge
- Absorbed attack from hooded figure
- Defended party from giant mantises and Astral Assassin
- Became inert when connection severed during battle
- Used for transportation and shelter in [World Below](#atlas/world-below)
- [Sylvie](#company/sylvie) cast Wall of Flame to warm it during blizzard

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
The Living Fortress serves as mobile transport, combat asset, and hidden storage. [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s use of [Phasing Vambraces](#relics/phasing-vambraces) to hide the [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch) inside makes it a crucial mission asset.

The pendant control mechanism may have limitations or vulnerabilities not yet discovered.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A dwarven pyre-keeper with a strong, stocky build typical of her kind. Maintains an attentive and careful demeanor when sharing knowledge about dangerous matters.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Sarru serves as pyre-keeper of the Sacred Pyre in [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step), an essential role for keeping the town warm and free from miasma. She maintains a connection with [Ygva](#personae/ygva), acting as a point of contact for those seeking guidance regarding the [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch).

sections.title: Role
sections.text:
- Tends the Sacred Pyre of [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step)
- Guardian and member of [Caul](#factions/caul)
- Point of contact for those seeking [Ygva](#personae/ygva)

sections.title: Abilities
sections.text:
- Knowledge of pyre maintenance and sacred rituals
- Combat capabilities as a Guardian
- Understanding of Umbra dangers

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text:
- **[Caul](#factions/caul)** - Member
- **[Ygva](#personae/ygva)** - Maintains connection, provides directions to seekers
- **[Savel](#personae/savel)** - Fellow party member
- **[Sylvie](#company/sylvie)** - Received protective wards from her

sections.title: Key Events
sections.text:
- Provided directions to [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s ruined shrine
- Warned party about physical and spiritual dangers of the path
- Joined return party into caverns with [Savel](#personae/savel), [Mellon](#personae/mellon), and [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)
- Received protective wards from [Sylvie](#company/sylvie) before descent
- Fought alongside party against hulking Umbra-corrupted brute
- Took damage from [Guardian](#personae/guardian) beast during battle
- Discovered Giant Collar with broken chain after battle
- Planned escort to [Drosven's Gate](#atlas/drosvens-gate) with blessed branches

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
Sarru represents the practical knowledge of maintaining civilization's defenses against the Umbra. Her role as pyre-keeper gives her unique insight into the sacred rituals and dangers involved.

She is loyal to both [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step) and [Caul](#factions/caul), potentially creating conflicts if their interests diverge.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A giant sorcerer known for his imposing stature and mastery of the arcane arts. His gauntleted fists reflect a blend of physical strength and magical prowess.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Savel is a member of [Caul](#factions/caul), working alongside the party to navigate hazardous environments and confront lurking threats. He has shown a mechanical aspect to his character, serving as both spellcaster and support.

sections.title: Abilities
sections.text:
- Arcane magic (strikes that can stagger large creatures)
- Protective magic for allies
- Physical combat with gauntleted fists
- Communication with spirits ([Mellon](#personae/mellon)'s ghost)

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text:
- **[Caul](#factions/caul)** - Member
- **[Sarru](#personae/sarru)** - Fellow party member
- **[Mellon](#personae/mellon)** - Communicated with his ghost
- **[Jamal](#company/jamal), [Draz](#company/draz)** - Traveled with them to Drosven's Gate
- Hinted ties to a witch (suggested by [Jamal](#company/jamal))

sections.title: Key Events
sections.text:
- Fought hulking goblinoid corrupted by Umbra in caverns
- Delivered arcane strikes that staggered the brute
- Communicated with [Mellon](#personae/mellon)'s ghost to learn his intent
- Facilitated movement of [Explosive Barrels](#relics/explosive-barrels) against [Guardian](#personae/guardian) beast
- Used [Mellon](#personae/mellon)'s ghost as distraction during battle
- Cast protective magic for [Jamal](#company/jamal)
- Planned escort to [Drosven's Gate](#atlas/drosvens-gate) with blessed branches

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
Savel's connection to a witch (hinted by [Jamal](#company/jamal)) suggests deeper ties to the supernatural forces at play. His ability to communicate with [Mellon](#personae/mellon)'s ghost indicates familiarity with spirits.

As a giant, he may have knowledge of [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step)'s history as a titan settlement originally founded by his kind.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A Celsian itinerant scholar with an academic demeanor. Currently serves as a tutor for children in [Verrow's Span](#atlas/verrows-span).

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Former initiate at the [Celsian Athenaeum](#atlas/celsian-athenaeum), Tamber possesses knowledge of ancient lore, especially the age of titans that predates civilization. She and [Ygva](#personae/ygva) learned from the same mentors but diverged in their practices—[Ygva](#personae/ygva) was expelled for using depletion (essence-draining), which contradicts Celsian ethics.

When [Ygva](#personae/ygva) returned, Tamber referred to her as "sister," while [Ygva](#personae/ygva) called her "apostate."

sections.title: Abilities & Knowledge
sections.text:
- Ancient history and titan age lore
- Runes and mystical texts
- Knowledge of the [Rune of the Moon](#relics/rune-of-the-moon) (false hope, paralysis of thought, [Kreth](#personae/kreth))
- Understanding of [Old Gods](#factions/old-gods) and their potential return
- Insight into magical artifacts and their origins

sections.title: Role
sections.text: Tamber serves as a source of scholarly knowledge for the party, particularly regarding [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s background and the nature of magical artifacts.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text:
- **[Ygva](#personae/ygva)** - Former peer; complex relationship ("sister"/"apostate")
- **[Sylvie](#company/sylvie)** - Examined her necklace and artifacts
- **[Heyou](#company/heyou)** - Invited him to study
- **[Draz](#company/draz)** - Explained his amulet's origins and limitations

sections.title: Key Insights Provided
sections.text:
- [Draz](#company/draz)'s amulet was commissioned by [God-King Otheidas](#personae/god-king-otheidas) to protect lesser mages from divine threats
- The amulet will NOT protect against [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s Umbra magic
- [Ygva](#personae/ygva) was expelled from Athenaeum for practicing depletion
- Mountain glyphs are remnants from the titan age
- The [Askavir](#personae/askavir) is potentially tied to [Tlellic](#personae/tlellic)

sections.title: Key Events
sections.text:
- Examined [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)'s artifacts but didn't recognize their make
- Revealed critical information about [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s history
- Rebuffed [Draz](#company/draz)'s proposal to support return of [Old Gods](#factions/old-gods)
- Adjusted teachings to caution against destabilizing ideas
- Expressed private concerns about [Draz](#company/draz)'s ambitions

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
Tamber represents orthodox scholarly tradition versus [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s heretical practices. She may possess hidden knowledge useful to the party but prioritizes social stability over grand changes.

Her warning about the [Old Gods](#factions/old-gods)' return suggests deeper knowledge of the dangers involved in [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s plan.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A large winged lion with a savage appearance and large, powerful wings allowing flight. His presence is bone-shaking, capable of instilling fear with his roar.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Valghast serves as mount and companion to [Ygva](#personae/ygva). He is linked to the deity [Mollthain](#personae/mollthain), known as The Rampart, indicating divine origins. He assists in travel between the upper world and the [World Below](#atlas/world-below).

sections.title: Abilities
sections.text:
- Flight with powerful wings
- Travel between realms (upper world and [World Below](#atlas/world-below))
- Communication (interpreted by [Draz](#company/draz) using Nature's Tongue)
- Fearsome roar
- May have connection to dream communication

sections.title: Role
sections.text: Crucial link between the party and [Ygva](#personae/ygva), providing transportation and assistance. Remains at sites to retrieve the party if necessary.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text:
- **[Ygva](#personae/ygva)** - Master/companion
- **[Mollthain](#personae/mollthain)** - Divine connection
- **[Draz](#company/draz)** - Communicated with via Nature's Tongue

sections.title: Key Events
sections.text:
- Landed at Moon Rune Carving with bone-shaking roar
- Agreed to take party to meet [Ygva](#personae/ygva)
- Transported party on [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s orders:
- Through "hole in the sky" to cavern ledge
- Near waterfall to aid exit from tunnels
- Remained at site to assist party with travel needs

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
Valghast's connection to [Mollthain](#personae/mollthain) suggests he may have abilities or knowledge beyond simple transportation. His loyalty to [Ygva](#personae/ygva) appears absolute.

As a divine creature, he may be able to sense things others cannot or have restrictions on his actions based on divine mandates.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A 7.5-foot witch of formidable presence and supernatural abilities. She wields a staff that enables manipulation of celestial forces, creating cloud alignments and knotwork. Known for her overwhelming force and tactical awareness.

sections.title: Background
sections.text:
Ygva was once a student at the [Celsian Athenaeum](#atlas/celsian-athenaeum) but was expelled for practicing essence-draining magic (depletion) that conflicted with the tenets of the archivists. This established a rift with [Tamber](#personae/tamber), her former peer, who calls her "apostate" while Ygva calls Tamber "sister."

She now resides near a mountainside shrine near [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step), drawing her power from the Umbra. Locals avoid her due to her strange habits and the dangers inherent in seeking her out.

sections.title: Abilities
sections.text:
- Teleportation (can bring others with her)
- Summoning misty/umbral entities
- Moonbeam attacks
- Hovering over water
- Staff-based celestial manipulation
- Dream communication with [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)
- Travel through rock, creating direct paths

sections.title: Goals
sections.text:
- Gather remnants and totems of the gods
- Light a colossal pyre to summon the gods
- Bind the gods in the [World Below](#atlas/world-below)
- Restore the world through the return of the gods

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text:
- **[Sylvie](#company/sylvie)** - Tore out her heart; now considers her a "sister" in Umbra magic
- **[Tamber](#personae/tamber)** - Former peer from the Athenaeum; calls her "apostate"
- **[Valghast](#personae/valghast)** - Her winged lion mount
- **[Kelun](#personae/kelun)** - Stone figure who compels others to seek her

sections.title: Key Events
sections.text:
- Teleported into confrontation with party, attacking with moonbeam
- Struck [Sylvie](#company/sylvie) in the heart, teleported away with her unconscious body
- Revealed cosmic truths to [Sylvie](#company/sylvie) about reality being an "egg" for cosmic entities
- Tore out [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)'s heart when [Draz](#company/draz) attacked during negotiations
- Later allied with party, accepting seed trade for [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch)
- Taught [Sylvie](#company/sylvie) the Summon Horror discipline
- Transported party on [Valghast](#personae/valghast) to aid their mission

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
Ygva's plan to bind the gods represents a potentially world-changing event. Her relationship with the party has shifted from antagonist to uneasy ally. She possesses [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)'s heart, which may be among offerings for the gods.

Her loneliness and ambition drive her—she claims her vision is not shared by many. The party's cooperation may be genuine or purely transactional.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A dead ranger who persists as a ghost. Accompanied by a cat companion named Yuki.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: Mellon was a ranger in life. The circumstances of his death are unclear, but his spirit lingers, encountered by the party on a bridge.

sections.title: Relationships
sections.text:
- **Yuki** - His cat companion, still present with him
- **[Kelun](#personae/kelun)** - The stone being shapeshifted into Mellon's form at one point, causing confusion

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text: Mellon's ghost represents the dangers of death in this world -- the risk of soul blight and undeath. His continued presence with Yuki adds a melancholy human element. [Kelun](#personae/kelun) using his form suggests the divine powers are aware of and can mimic the dead.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: A scholarly faction focused on preservation and study of magical knowledge, particularly arcane arts. Maintains rigorous standards and practices.

sections.title: Location
sections.text: Far to the west (exact location unspecified).

sections.title: Philosophy
sections.text:
- Responsible use of magic
- Archivism and preservation
- Alignment with teachings of powerful mentors
- Opposition to essence-draining practices (depletion)

sections.title: Training
sections.text: Initiates are trained in various forms of magic under strict ethical guidelines. Practices that drain magical essence are forbidden.

sections.title: Notable Members
sections.text: - **[Tamber](#personae/tamber)** - A fully-initiated Celsian itinerant in good standing; holds advanced techniques [Ygva](#personae/ygva) never learned

sections.title: Notable Former Members
sections.text:
- **[Ygva](#personae/ygva)** - Expelled before completing initiation for "depletion": draining an entity's entire essence to power a single effect, in violation of the Athenaeum's preservation ethos

Both [Tamber](#personae/tamber) and [Ygva](#personae/ygva) learned from the same mentors but diverged in practices. When they reunite, [Tamber](#personae/tamber) calls [Ygva](#personae/ygva) "apostate" while [Ygva](#personae/ygva) calls [Tamber](#personae/tamber) "sister."

sections.title: Relationship to Party
sections.text:
- [Tamber](#personae/tamber) serves as information source about [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s background
- Knowledge of [Otheidas](#personae/god-king-otheidas) relics and their properties
- Understanding of runes and mystical texts

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
The Athenaeum represents orthodox magical tradition versus the heretical practices of [Ygva](#personae/ygva). [Tamber](#personae/tamber) — who completed initiation where [Ygva](#personae/ygva) did not — embodies the tradition [Ygva](#personae/ygva) betrayed.

The faction may have further role if the party seeks magical knowledge or assistance against [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s plans. Their stance against the [Old Gods](#factions/old-gods)' return (via [Tamber](#personae/tamber)'s warnings) positions them as potential opposition to [Ygva](#personae/ygva)'s scheme.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Wandering educators who travel between settlements, spreading knowledge and preserving learning in a world where communities are isolated. Connected to the [Celsian Athenaeum](#atlas/celsian-athenaeum).

sections.title: Activities
sections.text:
- Traveling between settlements to teach
- Preserving pre-Apostasy knowledge
- Serving as messengers and cultural bridges between isolated communities

sections.title: Key Members
sections.text: - **[Tamber](#personae/tamber)** - A former initiate of the [Celsian Athenaeum](#atlas/celsian-athenaeum)

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text: The Celsian teachers serve as a connective tissue between the scattered settlements of The Enduring. They can be used as plot devices for delivering news, lore, or quest hooks from distant locations.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Relic hunters who explore dangerous ruins from the time before the Apostasy. They venture into Umbra-touched territory in search of artifacts, knowledge, and resources from the fallen Halcyon Domain.

sections.title: Activities
sections.text:
- Exploring ruins and abandoned settlements
- Recovering pre-Apostasy artifacts and technology
- Navigating areas beyond the reach of sacred pyres

sections.title: Connections
sections.text:
- Overlap with the [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers), who also scavenge from ruins
- Some Celsians may support or employ Delvers for scholarly purposes

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text: Delvers represent the adventuring class of this world -- those who risk the Umbra for profit or purpose. They can serve as quest-givers, rivals, or sources of information about ruins the party might explore.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: A powerful faction deeply entrenched in the criminal underworld, known for operations in the shadows and intricate ties to various illicit activities. Their reputation instills caution among local populations.

sections.title: Structure
sections.text: Network of semi-independent members operating across multiple settlements. Members identify each other through subtle signals and wear emblems like two-finger rings.

sections.title: Operations
sections.text:
- Trade and negotiation
- Acquisition of rare items (including essence of individuals)
- Infiltration and manipulation
- Information brokering

sections.title: Presence
sections.text:
- [Salthewn](#atlas/salthewn) - Hometown of [Heyou](#company/heyou), includes [Ugg](#personae/ugg) and [Grug](#personae/grug) (giant enforcers)
- [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step) - [Borek](#personae/borek) is local leader
- [Verrow's Span](#atlas/verrows-span) - Semi-independent operators present

sections.title: Key Members
sections.text:
- **[Borek](#personae/borek)** - Leader of [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step) operations, flamboyant dwarf
- **[Heyou](#company/heyou)** - Party member, former fence
- **[Ugg](#personae/ugg) & [Grug](#personae/grug)** - Giant twin enforcers from [Salthewn](#atlas/salthewn)
- Tall feline katari with eye patch among [Dolm's Break](#atlas/dolms-break) refugees

sections.title: Notable Dealings
sections.text:
- [Borek](#personae/borek) bargained [Askavir](#personae/askavir) eggs for information about [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s missing limbs
- [Borek](#personae/borek) possesses part of [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s essence, demands [Askavir](#personae/askavir) ink
- Party infiltrated [Borek](#personae/borek)'s quarters during distraction

sections.title: Reputation
sections.text: Grim incidents have marred their image (two members fell from high bridge). They are both recognized and regarded with suspicion in settlements where they operate.

sections.title: Heyou's Knowledge of Dimmers Subsets
sections.text:
"Dimmers" is a catch-all term for multiple, semi-overlapping groups that are scavenging from the ruins of the Halcyon Domain. Some are taking scarce [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch)es to light their way into temple and palace ruins for delving; others are more interested in getting a leg up on other survivors.

[Heyou](#company/heyou) has had direct interactions with two subsets:

1. **The Reactivators** - Interested in reactivating old stone clanks

2. **The Recyclers** - Focused on recycling found and stolen materials

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
The [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) represent the criminal element the party must navigate. [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s membership provides access but also obligations.

[Borek](#personae/borek)'s possession of part of [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s essence creates leverage and potential plot hooks. The infiltration into his quarters may have consequences.

The katari with eye patch among refugees warrants watching—likely a [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) operator with hidden agenda.

The Dimmers may be the same organization as (or a subset of) [The Syndicate](#factions/syndicate).

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: A faction of goblins recognized for mechanical expertise and engineering skills. Operate within [Underground Complex](#atlas/underground-complex), specializing in constructing defenses and explosive contraptions.

sections.title: Equipment
sections.text:
- Tool belts
- Socket wrenches
- Explosive barrels (three-part design)
- Focus on engineering over traditional combat

sections.title: Culture
sections.text:
- Pragmatic attitude toward workplace hazards
- Accept injuries as normal part of trade
- Dangerous approach to survival
- Willing to embrace chaos in pursuit of goals

sections.title: Tactics
sections.text:
- Utilize explosives to secure territory
- Rig defensive positions with explosive barrels
- Ambush intruders in tunnel systems
- Territory marked by ring of corpses

sections.title: Relationship with Party
sections.text:
- Established positive rapport with [Heyou](#company/heyou) (respected his mechanical aptitude)
- Goblin Envoy proposed alliance against [Guardian](#personae/guardian) beast
- Provided explosive powder as gesture of goodwill
- Alliance ended catastrophically when goblin accident destroyed [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex)

sections.title: Key Events
sections.text:
- Explained three-part explosive barrel design (shake, throw, detonate)
- Previous attempts against [Guardian](#personae/guardian) resulted in no returns
- Goblin carrying barrel caused catastrophic explosion
- Explosion destroyed [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex) and ended alliance hopes

sections.title: Casualties
sections.text: Multiple goblins killed in the accidental explosion, including the one carrying the barrel.

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
The [Goblin Engineers](#factions/goblin-engineers) represent a faction whose pragmatism led to disaster. Their destruction of the [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex) angered [Kelun](#personae/kelun) and the divine powers.

Despite the catastrophe, surviving engineers may still operate in the tunnels. Their engineering knowledge and explosive supplies could be valuable—or dangerous—in future encounters.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Ancient deities whose influence persists through relics, sacred rituals, and scattered followers. Their worship is considered heresy in contemporary society.

sections.title: The Veiled Gods (Otheidas and the Pantheon)
sections.text:
**Ulmira - Pacts, the Alliance between the Earth and the Heavens**

- [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step) was named as the first step of a forgotten pilgrimage in her honor
- Associated with pacts and divine covenants

**Tlellic - The Long Night, Predation**

- The [Askavir](#personae/askavir) is his mount/avatar (rumored to have been his familiar)
- Connected to Moon Rune (false hope, paralysis of thought)
- His departure left the [Askavir](#personae/askavir) as a remnant

**Kreth - False Visions, Deceit, The Moon**

- Associated with deception and lunar influence
- Connection to "Sister Moon" and Sylvie's powers is unexplored

**Brathis - Feral Survival, Loss of Personhood**

- Represents the degradation of civilized identity
- Survival at the cost of one's humanity

**Mollthain - The Rampart, Sturdy Against All Odds**

- Left great creatures in places like [Grithmaar Deep](#atlas/grithmaar-deep)
- One such creature destroyed [Jamal](#company/jamal)'s village
- [Valghast](#personae/valghast) (Ygva's lion) is linked to Mollthain

**Caranthalis - The Tree of Light, Source of Blessed Branches**

- God of the [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex)s and source of [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch)es
- [Kelun](#personae/kelun) primarily speaks for him
- Destruction of [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex) angered divine powers

**Ossa - The Wanderer Atop the Peaks**

- [Draz](#company/draz)'s compass points toward this god
- [Kelun](#personae/kelun) has served Ossa

**Otheidas - The Arrested Cycle of Life and Undeath, Revenants**

- Associated with cycles of life and undeath
- Relics protect lesser mages from divine powers
- [Draz](#company/draz)'s amulet and [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)'s circlet are connected to him
- [Celsians](#factions/celsians) preserve knowledge of his teachings

sections.title: Sacred Elements
sections.text:
- [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch)es for rekindling sacred pyres
- Sacred Pyres as defense against Umbra
- Altars throughout the world
- [Askavir](#personae/askavir) heart contains Splendor magic

sections.title: Ygva's Plan
sections.text:
[Ygva](#personae/ygva) seeks to bind the [Old Gods](#factions/old-gods) in the [World Below](#atlas/world-below) by:

- Gathering remnants and totems
- Constructing massive pyre with titans' help
- Using god-touched artifacts

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
The [Old Gods](#factions/old-gods) represent a cosmological framework the party is increasingly entangled with. [Draz](#company/draz) sought to recruit [Tamber](#personae/tamber) to revive them, but she refused citing social stability risks.

[Sylvie](#company/sylvie)'s transformation connects her to Umbra magic, which operates outside the [Old Gods](#factions/old-gods)' divine framework—or perhaps draws from the same source in different form.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Those who maintain the sacred fires that protect settlements from the Umbra. A vital role in every community that possesses a sacred pyre.

sections.title: Key Members
sections.text: - **[Sarru](#personae/sarru)** - Pyre-keeper of [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step)

sections.title: Responsibilities
sections.text:
- Maintaining and tending sacred pyres
- Ensuring the fire never goes out
- Procuring [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch)es when needed
- Guarding against threats to the pyre

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text: The pyre-keepers represent the thin line between survival and annihilation for most settlements. Their knowledge of how pyres work -- and their limitations -- makes them important sources of information.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: A term used by the extant communities that have survived the Apostasy and the coming of the Umbra. Not a formal organization so much as a shared identity among the scattered settlements that persist under the protection of sacred pyres.

sections.title: Member Settlements
sections.text:
- [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step)
- [Drosven's Gate](#atlas/drosvens-gate)
- [Salthewn](#atlas/salthewn)
- [Thistleglass](#atlas/thistleglass)
- [Verrow's Span](#atlas/verrows-span)

sections.title: Characteristics
sections.text:
- Settlements are scattered and operate semi-independently
- United by shared reliance on sacred pyres and [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch)es
- Each community has developed its own culture, dialect, and survival strategies

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text: The Enduring is the campaign's namesake. The "Lesser Lights" likely refers to the sacred pyres themselves -- lesser lights that keep the darkness at bay in the absence of the gods.

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: A criminal organization active in multiple cities. [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s background is tied to the Syndicate. May overlap with or be an alternate name for the [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) network.

sections.title: Operations
sections.text:
- Active across multiple settlements
- Criminal enterprise with wide-reaching influence

sections.title: Key Members
sections.text:
- **[Borek](#personae/borek)** - Syndicate dwarf in [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step) who knows about [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s missing limbs
- **[Heyou](#company/heyou)** - Connected through his background

sections.title: Notable Dealings
sections.text:
- [Borek](#personae/borek) requested [Askavir](#personae/askavir) eggs
- The party stole back [Heyou](#company/heyou)'s leg from [Borek](#personae/borek)'s home

sections.title: Connections to PCs
sections.text: - [Draz](#company/draz) has interacted with Syndicate runners through the forest glade; this may be his only connection to the outside world

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text: The Syndicate and [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers) may be the same organization referred to by different names, or the Syndicate may be the larger parent organization of which the Dimmers are a subset. Clarify as the campaign develops.

sections.title: Description
sections.text:
An immense raptor with an extraordinary wingspan of nearly ninety feet and talons marking it as a being of divine origin. Its silhouette casts a vast shadow over the landscape. Possesses intelligence and agency surpassing typical animal behavior.

The name "Askavir" comes from the Lammat dialect spoken by the Kurael of [Ulmira's Step](#atlas/ulmiras-step). When alive, it appeared rarely -- at most once per month -- seen in silhouette against the clouds or moon. Its presence inspired awe and fear but it rarely attacked the Step directly. Rumored to have been the familiar of the Veiled God [Tlellic](#personae/tlellic).

sections.title: Divine Connection
sections.text: The Askavir is tied to [Tlellic](#personae/tlellic), the god of predation. Its purpose involves finding and delivering specific individuals under divine mandates connected to greater cosmic forces.

sections.title: Abilities
sections.text:
- Flight with 90-foot wingspan
- Communication through Nature's Tongue
- Divine mandate to capture specific individuals
- Powerful wing beats that shake structures
- Talons capable of lifting humanoids
- Splendor magic emanating from heart

sections.title: Combat Behavior
sections.text:
- Swoops to capture targets
- Can lift and drop victims from height
- Bites can bisect a humanoid
- Wing beats create environmental hazards
- Heart contains overwhelming Splendor magic

sections.title: Key Events
sections.text:
- Captured [Jamal](#company/jamal) and [Draz](#company/draz), dropping them on separate peaks
- Shook rope bridge with wing beats
- Attacked [Verrow's Span](#atlas/verrows-span), capturing refugees
- Tethered by [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)'s magic, crashed onto ledge
- Shot in eye by [Draz](#company/draz)
- Set ablaze by [Sylvie](#company/sylvie)'s Fireball
- Died thrashing in the plaza

sections.title: Remains & Value
sections.text:
- Heart: Potent Splendor magic, overwhelming to siphon
- Eggs: Valuable, sought by [Borek](#personae/borek) and [Dimmers](#factions/dimmers)
- Ink: Demanded by [Borek](#personae/borek)
- Claws: [Heyou](#company/heyou) forged a dagger from one
- Eyes: [Sylvie](#company/sylvie) took them for her bag
- Bones: [Draz](#company/draz)'s kinfolk to tend them

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
Though dead, the Askavir's remains hold significant value and power. Its connection to [Tlellic](#personae/tlellic) means its death may have divine consequences.

The heart's Splendor magic was too overwhelming for [Sylvie](#company/sylvie) to siphon—it may require special circumstances or preparation to utilize. [Heyou](#company/heyou) absorbed a portion, gaining holy power.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A purple, multi-eyed, feline-like demon tethered to a [Glowing Tree](#atlas/underground-complex). Features a Giant Collar with a broken chain indicating prior connection to a [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex). Produces gray, extremely cold viscous fluid.

sections.title: Abilities
sections.text:
- Unnatural intellect and calculated hostility
- Tactical repositioning during combat
- Grappling ability to ensnare targets from distance
- Held [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch) in its mouth

sections.title: Combat Behavior
sections.text:
- Behaves with calculated hostility toward intruders
- Intelligent repositioning complicates opponents' strategies
- Can grapple from unexpected distances
- Responses to Nature's Tongue were hostile

sections.title: Origin
sections.text: Appears to be a corrupted or summoned being, bound to protect the [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex). The broken chain on its collar suggests it was once more securely tethered.

sections.title: Key Events
sections.text:
- Discovered at [Glowing Tree](#atlas/underground-complex) holding [Blessed Branch](#relics/blessed-branch)
- [Draz](#company/draz) attempted communication via Nature's Tongue—received hostility
- Goblin Envoy proposed alliance against it
- Party used [Explosive Barrels](#relics/explosive-barrels) in assault
- [Draz](#company/draz) fired arrow at barrels, freeing beast from tether
- Sustained severe injuries from explosions
- [Jamal](#company/jamal) crushed its paw with warhammer
- [Heyou](#company/heyou) decapitated it with daggers
- [Sarru](#personae/sarru) took damage from its attack

sections.title: Aftermath
sections.text:
- Party discovered burnt and regrown [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex)
- Found Giant Collar with broken chain
- Raised questions about what bound the Guardian to the tree

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
The Guardian was bound to the [Sacred Tree](#atlas/underground-complex) by forces connected to [Caranthalis](#personae/caranthalis). Its death (and the subsequent destruction of the tree by goblins) angered [Kelun](#personae/kelun) and the divine powers.

The cold viscous fluid and multi-eyed appearance suggest Umbra corruption or demonic origin.

sections.title: Description
sections.text: A ten-foot-tall creature that emerges from stone walls. Connected to ancient technology and supernatural elements.

sections.title: Abilities
sections.text:
- Emerges from solid stone
- Resistance to conventional weaponry (arrows pushed back)
- Subsonic attacks that disrupt environment
- Can knock opponents off perches
- Causes falling rocks
- Retaliation against ranged attacks

sections.title: Combat Behavior
sections.text:
- Attacks produce deep subsonic rumbles
- Can target multiple enemies through environmental effects
- Conventional weapons are largely ineffective

sections.title: Communication
sections.text: Can respond to peaceful approach. [Sylvie](#company/sylvie) approached with open hands and received attentive response.

sections.title: Ancient Connection
sections.text:
The spirit within a Stonewraith can temporarily inhabit other beings. One possessed [Heyou](#company/heyou), revealing:

- It had roamed the area for thirty years
- Warned about the [Guardian](#personae/guardian) of the [Glowing Tree](#atlas/underground-complex)
- Connected to a magical relay system

sections.title: Encounters
sections.text:
- [Draz](#company/draz)'s arrow was pushed back by its defenses
- Subsonic attack caused falling rocks damaging [Draz](#company/draz)
- [Heyou](#company/heyou) was temporarily possessed, learning vital information

sections.title: GM Notes
sections.text:
Stonewraiths appear to be guardians or observers connected to ancient systems. They're not necessarily hostile if approached correctly, but will defend against perceived threats.

Their connection to [Heyou](#company/heyou) (who recognized it as ancient tech) suggests clanks and Stonewraiths may share origins.

pc.title: Draft — Sylvie Cerridwen
pc.text:
**Name:** Sylvie Cerridwen

**Ancestry:** Human

**Age:** Early 40s

**Class:** Witch (Wizard)

**Community:** Ridgeborne (specifically, from the now-destroyed Stoneheart Peaks) **Specialization:** School of Knowledge

**Core Concept:** Sylvie was a Stoneweaver from an isolated, mountain community dedicated to containing an ancient magical nexus. A profound conflict with a powerful colleague, whose insidious magical manipulations escalated into an attempt to dominate and violate her magical channels, led to a cataclysmic confrontation. This event, known as the "Sundering of the Stoneheart," resulted in the destruction of her home and the irreversible transformation of her magic from earth-attuned to lunar. She now wields potent, moon-infused magic, bearing the indelible marks of this destructive transformation.

**Daggerheart Mechanics:**

- **Hope:** To find a new purpose where her unique understanding of magic can be valuable, and to prevent widespread destruction or imbalance caused by unchecked power.
- **Fear:** That the power she was forced to unleash will consume her, or that she might inadvertently cause similar widespread devastation.
- **Experiences:**
- **Sister Moon:** Reflects a heightened magical potency under direct moonlight, allowing her to push limits or perceive hidden truths related to lunar energies.
- **The Scarred Earth:** Represents the profound loss of her home and her intuitive understanding of corruption, destruction, or fragmented magic, particularly regarding geological or elemental forces.

sections.title: Key Background & World-Building Elements for GM Agreement
sections.text:
The following elements form the foundation of Sylvie's character and would need to be integrated into the game world's lore and geography.

- **The Stoneheart Peaks & The Ridgeborne Community:** An ancient, isolated human community nestled deep within the mountains. This community, specifically the Stoneheart Peaks settlement, is now **destroyed/sundered/ruined** due to a cataclysmic magical event.
- **The Stoneweaver Order & The Earth-Heart:**
- **The Stoneweavers:** An ancient, hereditary magical order within the Stoneheart Peaks. Their magic was traditionally earth-attuned, focused on harmony, containment, and subtle manipulation of mountain energies.
- **The Earth-Heart:** A **profound, ancient, primal nexus of magic** hidden deep within the Stoneheart Peaks. It is a vast, powerful entity whose immense, raw energy requires constant guardianship.
- **The Five Guardians:** Only five Stoneweavers (Sylvie, Kaelen, Rhys, and two others) were entrusted with its guardianship, performing the **Confluence Ritual** to contain its volatile power.
- **Kaelen & Rhys:**
- **Kaelen:** A powerful Stoneweaver whose ambition led him to seek absolute control over the Earth-Heart. He engaged in **insidious magical and psychological manipulations** directed at Sylvie, attempting to destabilize her connection to the Earth-Heart and gain dominance.
- **Rhys:** A Stoneweaver and Sylvie's peer who, despite understanding Kaelen's problematic actions, chose to prioritize Kaelen's promises of power for the order over intervening to support Sylvie, remaining silent and complicit.
- **The Sundering of the Stoneheart:**
- **The Event:** A cataclysmic magical confrontation during the sacred Confluence Ritual. Kaelen's escalating magical assault and his attempt to directly **control and violate Sylvie's magical channels** triggered Sylvie's forceful, newly awakened lunar magic.
- **The Cataclysm:** The resulting clash of unleashed power between Sylvie and Kaelen, combined with Kaelen's previous manipulations and the compromised state of the Earth-Heart, caused the **Sundering of the Stoneheart**, destroying the mountain settlement (and much of the mountain itself). Occasional survivors may be encountered. The surviving members of her community, if any found her, would likely view her as a destructive force, a pariah responsible for their ruin.
- **The Fates of the Five Stoneweavers:**
- **Kaelen:** Was **utterly obliterated** by Sylvie's power, leaving no trace.
- **Rhys:** Was **trapped within the fractured remnants of the Earth-Heart** in a unique magical stasis/prison, a living consequence of his choices.
- **The Other Two:** Were **lost to the immediate cataclysm** and are presumed dead.
- **Sylvie's New Magic (Lunar Weaving) & Magical Items:**
- **Shift in Power:** Sylvie's old earth-attuned Stoneweaver magic was irrevocably severed. Her new power is entirely **lunar-based**, manifesting from a profound connection to the "Sister Moon."
- **The Staff of Sundered Moonlight:** Her magical two-handed staff was **forged in the chaos of the Sundering**. An ancient tree branch, steeped in the Peaks' energy, became infused with her raw lunar magic, transforming into a staff dense as petrified wood, pulsing with inner moonlight and silver veins.
- **The Whispering Deck:** A cherished tarot deck, a gift from her **grandmother** (a previous Stoneweaver). Sylvie had it on her person during the Sundering, and it was imbued with the chaotic lunar energies, becoming a living link to her past and a transformed magical artifact. It is used for **meditation and unlocking magical insight**.
- **Knowledge Acquisition:** She studies moon magic through meticulous direct observation of the moon and magical experimentation, compiling insights into her **grimoire. ** She also seeks out **forgotten lore scraps**, insights from oral history traditions, ancient runes from forgotten days, trying to piece together what the wild magic is that speaks to her now.
- **Flint:** Sylvie's crow familiar. He served as a silent witness during the time of Kaelen's manipulations and now remains her loyal companion.
- **Sylvie's Lunar Weavings:** She knits, especially under moonlight, weaving silent protective spells and lunar blessings into the fabric. These charm-infused knitted items are often given to those she perceives as vulnerable.

sections.title: GM Response
sections.text:
1. As a Stoneweaver, mechanically you were once a level 5-7 sorcerer.,

2. What Kaelen did sundered the mountain, and tried to disempower you. Instead, you pushed your powers into the mountain itself. Kaelen & Rhys cast part of the mountain up to the moon.,

3. There was a period in which Sylvie was without magic, and she slowly began to relearn as she traveled between settlements, scraping together bits of lore.,

4. She learned that when she traveled in moonlight, she was generally able to travel safely.,

5. Some of the lore that she picked up related to practices of the old Veiled Gods (Splendor Domain). Oddly enough, the *practices* seem to work, even in the absence of divine connection

- I guess my question then is are Kaelen / Rhys dead then? Maybe not. If she was stripped of her power by events, then she presumably didn’t win that battle magically?
- She believes with a high degree of confidence that they are dead.

sections.title: Player questions:
sections.text:
Mechanism Explaining Sylvie's Moon Tie: A Convergence of Blood, Lore, and Cataclysm

Sylvie's profound and sudden connection to the Sister Moon is not a singular phenomenon but the culmination of several interwoven threads: a deeply ancient, almost forgotten aspect of Stoneweaver lore; a specific, powerful ancestral heritage; and the cataclysmic trauma of the Sundering itself.

- The "Sister Moon" in Ancient Earth-Heart Lore (Earth-Heart's True Nature): While the dominant Stoneweaver tradition focused solely on the Earth-Heart's terrestrial power, deeper, more archaic texts within their sacred lore spoke of a complementary force: the "Sister Moon." This wasn't merely the celestial body, but a recognized cosmic counterpart to the Earth-Heart's primal energy, representing balance, cycles, unseen currents, and receptive power – an ethereal yin to the Earth-Heart's grounded yang. Over millennia, as the Stoneweavers became increasingly pragmatic in their containment duties, this lunar aspect faded into obscured metaphor, honored in name but rarely truly understood or actively engaged. It was a concept, a philosophical balance, rather than an accessible magical wellspring.,
- An Ancestral Lunar Heritage (Bloodline Revelation): Generations ago, Sylvie's grandmother's mother brought a unique thread into the Cerridwen lineage when she married into the clan. She hailed from a hidden, ancient tradition (perhaps from a nomadic people, or a valley clan that revered celestial bodies), carrying a potent, latent affinity for lunar magic. This affinity was passed down through the generations, a quiet, almost imperceptible hum in the bloodline, lying dormant within most of her descendants, including Sylvie's grandmother and mother, as it lacked the specific trigger or environment to manifest. It was a seed that never fully bloomed within the earth-attuned environment of the Stoneheart Peaks.,
- The Catalyst of Cataclysmic Trauma (Latent Affinity Activated & Earth-Heart's Rebalancing): Sylvie herself, unbeknownst to her, carried this intensified, latent lunar affinity in her blood. Her own quiet, intuitive nature, while perfectly suited to earth-weaving, also inherently resonated with the subtle, introspective power of the moon. The truly transformative moment came during the Sundering. Kaelen's relentless, aggressive, and violating magic didn't just clash with Sylvie; it assaulted the very balance of the Earth-Heart itself. His attempts to dominate and force the ancient nexus, coupled with his profound violation of Sylvie's own magical channels, threw the entire system into an unprecedented, catastrophic disequilibrium. When Sylvie's traditional earth magic was irrevocably severed, unable to bear the combined assault and the betrayal, a void was created. In that moment of utter desperation and her defiant, primal "NO," the now-uncontained Earth-Heart, thrashing in its own self-preservation, instinctively sought balance. It resonated with the only other complementary force present in the immediate vicinity that also stood in pure opposition to Kaelen's aggressive intent: the ancient, dormant lunar affinity in Sylvie's very blood.,
- The Earth-Heart, bleeding its power, inadvertently or as a final act of re-equilibration, amplified and funneled its complementary lunar aspect directly into Sylvie. The extreme trauma and the complete magical severance acted as the violent "key," unlocking and igniting the powerful, inherited lunar magic that had lain dormant for generations. The "Sister Moon," as both a cosmic entity and a revered concept in ancient lore, answered the call, not just as a patron, but as an inherent magical force now directly connected to Sylvie's being.

In essence, Sylvie didn't just gain new magic; her ancient bloodline's dormant lunar potential was violently activated and magnified by the collapsing Earth-Heart's desperate lunge for balance, all triggered by Kaelen's destructive forces. She became a living, breathing testament to the interconnectedness of all primal forces and the unforeseen consequences of disrupting ancient harmonies.

sections.title: GM Response
sections.text:
Sylvie can think whatever she would like about it; I suspect the bulk of it more has to do with Kaelen & Rhys casting her power with a chunk of the mountain up to the moon.

But I also like the idea of the "Earth-heart" connecting to her, a godlike connection but one that is impersonal and inchoate.

I generally lean against "oh, it's in the protagonist's blood" explanations for things, but if that's important to you we can figure something out.
